name: Lynx
introduction: is the Lynx, named by Johannes Hevelius in 1687, who said that you would need the eyes of a lynx to see it. It is a long, faint chain of stars between the Great Bear and Auriga, best seen on dark northern winter and spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Only one star in Lynx has a Greek letter. [Alpha Lyncis](hip:45860), an orange-red giant about 220 light-years away, is the brightest.
Boundaries can be confusing: the star [10 Ursae Majoris](hip:44248), as its name says, was once part of the Great Bear but now lies in Lynx.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [38 Lyncis](hip:45688) is a pleasing double star, and [10 Ursae Majoris](hip:44248) is a binary of two Sun-like stars 61 light-years away.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Lynx contains the Intergalactic Wanderer, NGC 2419, a globular cluster about 300,000 light-years away, farther than the Magellanic Clouds.
